newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits outlook - 10-year note sale.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits outlook - 10-year note sale.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in moderate trade on Wednesday, dealers said.

They said most traders were sidelined ahead of the U.S. Treasury's sale of US$12.0 billion 10-year notes, the last leg of the two-part quarterly refunding. The Treasury sold US$17.0 billion three-year notes on Tuesday.

"The market was quiet and featureless on lack of fresh factors. There was little impact from Tuesday's (U.S. Treasury) three-year note sale and (March) factory orders figures and most people are sitting on the sidelines," a local dealer said.
"Demand for Tuesday's (U.S. Treasury) three-year notes sale was moderate but some people are waiting for the outcome of tonight's 10-year note sale," he said.

The market is also waiting for possible direction from the U.S. first quarter productivity/unit labor costs, March wholesale inventories, Federal Beige Book survey and March consumer credit data due later today, but they will probably be non-events," another dealer said.
In short dates, Wednesday/Thursday, Thursday/Friday and week-fixed were unchanged from Tuesday's common 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent, respectively.

Among term rates, one-month was unchanged from Tuesday's 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16, nine-months unchanged at 6-1/8 6 and twelve-months unchanged at 6-1/4 6-1/8 percent.
